title: Colour Lab: picker, editable code, live swatches, HEX/RGB/HSL synchronization, copyable snippets
learningObjectives: Explain colour lab: picker, editable code, live swatches, hex/rgb/hsl synchronization, copyable snippets and apply it correctly in a small CSS example.

understand.concept: A colour lab combines a colour picker with editable CSS values and a live preview. A robust tool keeps HEX, RGB, and HSL representations synchronized, validates user input, and makes the generated CSS easy to copy. The displayed formats represent the same selected colour, not three separate colours.
understand.whyItMatters: Use a native input type=color for a convenient picker, but do not assume it covers every alpha workflow. Parse and validate text input before updating the preview. Keep labels visible, announce validation errors, and avoid inserting user-entered text as HTML.
understand.analogy: A colour lab is like a control panel with three different readouts for one setting. Changing one readout should update the others without changing the underlying selected colour unexpectedly.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps build intuition, but the browser follows the CSS specifications and computed-style rules rather than human intentions.

explain.narrative: This small starter demonstrates a picker and HEX field staying synchronized with a live swatch. It intentionally validates six-digit HEX only; a production lab must also implement RGB/HSL conversion, alpha, accessible error feedback, and copy interaction.

practise.guidedTask: Extend the starter so valid HEX input updates RGB and HSL readouts. Add a copy button using the Clipboard API with permission-aware feedback. Test invalid input without changing the last valid preview.
practise.independentTask: Why should a colour lab validate text input before applying it to the preview?
hints: Change one CSS value at a time and observe the result.
Use browser developer tools to inspect the computed value.
Keep meaningful content in HTML; use CSS for presentation.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to learn the effect of a CSS value?
options: Change one value and inspect the rendered result
Add unrelated declarations until it looks right
Assume every browser calculates styles identically in every context
